name: llama.cpp backend performance varies dramatically: CUDA > Metal > Vulkan > CPU
symptom: The same GGUF model on the same hardware can run at wildly different speeds depending on the llama.cpp backend. CUDA is typically 2-5x faster than Metal, which is 2-5x faster than Vulkan, which is 2-5x faster than CPU.
root_cause: Each backend has different levels of optimization. CUDA benefits from NVIDIA's highly optimized kernels and tensor cores. Metal is well-optimized for Apple Silicon but has fewer kernels than CUDA. Vulkan is the universal fallback but is not optimized for any specific hardware. CPU is the baseline with AVX2/AVX512 optimizations but no GPU acceleration.
workaround: Always use the best available backend for your hardware: CUDA for NVIDIA GPUs, Metal for Apple Silicon, Vulkan for AMD/Intel GPUs. Check llama.cpp benchmarks for your specific hardware and model. Do not assume that a faster GPU always yields faster inference - the backend matters as much as the hardware.
notes: The backend hierarchy for llama.cpp: CUDA (NVIDIA) > Metal (Apple) > Vulkan (AMD/Intel) > CPU. The gap between backends can be 2-5x. For example, a 70B model at 4-bit on an RTX 4090 might run at 35 tokens/sec with CUDA but only 15 tokens/sec with Vulkan. On an M4 Max, Metal might yield 20 tokens/sec while Vulkan yields 8 tokens/sec. Always benchmark with the correct backend for your hardware.
